item.title: Claude Models Compared: Knowledge Cutoff, Pricing and Plans
item.description:
This guide compares the Claude models in the chat model menu: Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, plus the older versions under “More models”. It covers each model’s knowledge cutoff, strengths and pricing, the Effort setting, and the differences between the Free, Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans.

Every fact here comes from Anthropic’s own documentation, linked at the end. Figures are correct as of 8 October 2026.

Which Claude model should I use?

  • Sonnet 5.5 for most everyday chat: writing, editing, analysis.
  • Opus 5.5 for hard reasoning and long back-and-forth work.
  • Fable 5.1 for long tasks with many steps, or dense source material.
  • Haiku 5.5 for quick lookups and short summaries.
  • Leave effort on Default until you have a reason to change it.

item.title: The AI Toolkit for Research Institutions: Five Tools for 2026
item.description: The AI toolkit for research institutions in 2026 has five tools, not one. Each tool does a distinct job. NotebookLM combines your own documents into one summary. Claude writes text and creates visual outputs. ChatGPT gives broad task coverage and flexible integrations. Gemini does autonomous web research and creates visuals from data. Napkin.ai turns paragraphs into diagrams. Together, these tools cover the full knowledge work cycle from intake to output, and you do not need coding skills to use them.

item.title: How to Customise Your CV for Every Job Application Using Claude
item.description: One-size-fits-all CVs do not work. Hiring managers spend only seconds on each screening. Applicant tracking systems (ATS) filter applications by keyword match. True CV customization for each role takes time. It means you research the employer, understand the team context, and reframe your experience with strategy. Most people skip this step entirely. This guide shows you how to use Claude with structured approval gates. You can customize your CV for every application without losing authenticity or inventing experience.
